This example prepares hourly freeway flow in vehicles per hour for the Los Angeles and San Francisco Bay areas. The drawing input covers all 24 source hours of 16 June 2026. By default, the report shows the 08:00 hour for both regions. Diamonds mark when the California Highway Patrol (CHP) logged the start of an incident.

1 Set up the example

In an interactive R session, set the working directory to the folder containing this report and run the visible R blocks in order. The blocks use the installed bdynets package, the supplied PeMS and CHP files, and a temporary directory for the prepared tables. The YAML parameters control the plotted hour, offline street context and export.

prepare.R converts this case’s source records. The detector and event readers are in scripts/read-source.R. The local scripts/prepare-input.R aligns the road and time tables and writes the prepared RDS files. scripts/street-context.R reads the local background, and scripts/report-export.R saves the prepared data and static maps when export is requested.

library(bdynets)
source("scripts/prepare-input.R", local = TRUE)
source("prepare.R", local = TRUE)
source("scripts/report-export.R", local = TRUE)
source("scripts/street-context.R", local = TRUE)
if (!exists("params", inherits = FALSE)) {
  params <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter("pems-flow-report.Rmd")$params
}
data_dir <- "data"
work <- tempfile("pems-flow-report-")
dir.create(work)

The prepared input guide describes the final drawing object. For other source data, choose the fields, time intervals and conversion rules that fit that data.

2 Read the supplied data

The supplied files include Caltrans Station 5-Minute records from districts 04, 07, 08 and 12, dated D04 station metadata, and June CHP incident summaries and details. The bundled detector text preserves all 52 source columns in the selected rows for 16 June. The supplied CHP summaries contain starts on 16 June from the four districts, even though the source filename contains month. The detail file contains messages linked to those IDs, including messages posted after midnight. Preparation applies the two regional bounds to the supplied event coordinates.

The project reference files define the study roads and identify the detector positions used by the published series. The June flow manifest identifies active positions. The LA volume HTML maps each position to a detector ID. The source manifest records both names. Use the Path in this example column below to locate the files supplied with the example. Upstream file identifies the original source.

register_file <- file.path(data_dir, "case-register.rds")
raw <- file.path(data_dir, "raw")
files <- pems_files(file.path(raw, "caltrans"), file.path(raw, "reference"))
source_manifest <- read.csv(file.path(raw, "source-manifest.csv"))
source_manifest <- source_manifest[match(names(files), source_manifest$role), ]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  role = source_manifest$role,
  bundled_path = file.path(raw, source_manifest$file),
  upstream_file = source_manifest$source_file
), col.names = c("Role", "Path in this example", "Upstream file"), row.names = FALSE)

2.1 Inspect the case register and station links

The supplied case register preserves the link selections and travel-order decisions for the 16 June 2026 case from the 21 November handover. This report reads those settings from the included RDS. The input inventory lists the other references. The register stores the LA links whose endpoint order and geometry need to be reversed together, the selected D04 directed endpoint pairs, the event coordinate bounds and category lookup, and the 24 hour starts.

LA road geometry comes from the project volume HTML configuration. D04 road geometry connects the two endpoint coordinates from the dated Caltrans metadata, with the two detectors on the same freeway and direction. The D04 station-map CSV identifies the stations selected for the Bay Area. Match its station_id and the register’s endpoint IDs to ID in the station metadata.

selection <- pems_selection(register_file, files)
register <- selection$register
frame_times <- register$settings$times
register$origin["projection"]
## $projection
## [1] "Link-selection and travel-order decisions from the published 16 June 2026 case; geographic selection, category lookup and case settings."
data.frame(la_reversed_links = length(register$la_reverse_id),
           bay_directed_links = nrow(register$d04_links),
           event_type_mappings = nrow(register$event_categories),
           hour_starts = length(frame_times))
##   la_reversed_links bay_directed_links event_type_mappings hour_starts

The June key selects the active zero-based positions from the manifest. positionStations[position + 1] in the volume HTML configuration supplies the detector IDs. The selected positions and D04 station IDs determine which measurements enter the native matrices.

2.2 Read the source day and link the records

The detector reader retains the freeway mainline records for this case. The detector fields used here are V1 for the source clock, V2 for the detector ID, V3 for the district and V10 for the five-minute total vehicle count. Preparation checks that each daily timestamp belongs to one of the 288 five-minute slots on the case day. The numeric time keys encode the source clock, whose UTC offset is unspecified.

CHP summary fields 1 and 4 give the incident ID and start time, fields 10 and 11 give latitude and longitude, and field 12 gives the district. Preparation matches detail rows to summary IDs and counts the messages. For included LA starts it joins the supplied English events.csv by incident ID and checks its message count before using the English summary. Bay Area descriptions use the original summary fields. Coordinates put each start in one of three groups in the native table. Only starts marked inside enter the prepared event table; outside means valid coordinates outside the region, and invalid means bad coordinates.

observations <- pems_observations(files, frame_times)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  district = sub("detector", "", names(observations$records)),
  five_minute_rows = vapply(observations$records, nrow, integer(1L)),
  stations = vapply(observations$records, function(x) length(unique(x$V2)), integer(1L))
), row.names = FALSE)

3 Prepare the drawing input

For D04, add twelve five-minute counts for each detector and hour. For LA, sum the available five-minute counts at each active position, record the number of slots that contributed, and average the available position totals for each detector. An observed zero contributes to coverage. An LA position with no reading that hour stays missing.

The hourly road value is the mean of its available endpoint totals. One observed endpoint supplies the road value. Two missing endpoints yield a missing road-hour. The flow table in input.rds includes all roads and hours, including missing road-hours.

day_input <- pems_flow_input(native)
prepared_dir <- file.path(work, "prepared-data")
sources <- c(register_file, unname(files))
input_path <- write_pems_flow(native, day_input, prepared_dir, sources)
frames_path <- file.path(prepared_dir, "flow-frames.rds")
saved_input <- readRDS(input_path)
frames <- readRDS(frames_path)
clock <- as.POSIXct(frames$times, origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC")
hours <- format(clock, "%H:%M", tz = "UTC")
data.frame(roads = nrow(saved_input$roads), road_hours = nrow(saved_input$flow),
           hour_frames = length(hours), first = hours[1L], last = tail(hours, 1L),
           unit = saved_input$unit)
##   roads road_hours hour_frames first  last          unit
## 1  6638     159312          24 00:00 23:00 vehicles/hour
with(saved_input$provenance, data.frame(
  chp_starts = source_incidents, inside_bounds = included_incidents,
  outside_bounds = outside_scope, invalid_coordinates = invalid_coordinates
))
##   chp_starts inside_bounds outside_bounds invalid_coordinates
## 1       1023          1019              4                   0
File Contents
source.rds The native object tagged pems-flow-source-v1. It contains the selected hourly LA position counts and coverage, the D04 five-minute count matrix, directed roads, and the incident table with its source clock and scope.
input.rds The road, flow and prepared event tables, the 24 hour starts and provenance. Event times are numeric source-clock keys.
flow-frames.rds The roads and observations aligned into a drawing matrix with times in rows and roads in columns. Pass this object to the plotting function.

The preparation directory also contains roads.csv, road-vertices.csv, flow.csv and events.csv. data-dictionary.csv describes their fields. metadata.json records the clock, units and provenance, source-files.csv identifies the inputs, and checksums.csv identifies the outputs.

3.1 Trace the 08:00 flow values and a CHP start

The Bay Area example follows the two endpoint detectors of northbound US 101 road D04:101:N:400001:404753. The table shows their original five-minute counts and the two hourly totals. Their mean gives the flow saved for that road. LA link 0 uses the June project-position table to retrieve its endpoint totals. LA link 765 illustrates a road-hour with missing flow.

worked_index <- match("08:00", hours)
slots <- (worked_index - 1L) * 12L + seq_len(12L)
bay_road <- register$d04_links$road_id[1L]
bay_counts <- native$d04$counts[bay_pair, slots, drop = FALSE]
knitr::kable(data.frame(clock = substr(observations$labels[slots], 12L, 16L),
                        t(bay_counts), check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)

3.2 From the road table to the exact drawing input

The preparation writer takes every frame start in input.rds in order and every entry in roads$road_id in road-table order. Each observation is placed at values[match(time, times), match(road_id, roads$road_id)]. The matrix starts with NA cells, so missing road–time observations stay missing and observed zeros remain zero. The resulting object also carries the ordered road geometries, frame widths, units and any prepared events. Preparation saves that object as flow-frames.rds. This is the standard drawing input. input.rds is the earlier table export for inspecting or reusing the conversion.

observation <- saved_input$flow[saved_input$flow$road_id == register$d04_links$road_id[1L] & saved_input$flow$time == frames$times[worked_index], ]
row <- match(observation$time, frames$times)
column <- match(observation$road_id, frames$roads$road_id)
data.frame(road_id = observation$road_id, time = observation$time,
  time_row = row, road_column = column,
  value_in_input_table = observation$flow,
  value_in_drawing_matrix = frames$values[row, column])
##                   road_id       time time_row road_column value_in_input_table
## 1 D04:101:N:400001:404753 1781596800        9        4436                 4695
##   value_in_drawing_matrix
## 1                    4695
data.frame(frame_rows = nrow(frames$values),
  road_columns = ncol(frames$values), unit = frames$unit)
##   frame_rows road_columns          unit
## 1         24         6638 vehicles/hour

4 Draw the selected hour

The prepared input retains all 24 hourly starts from the case register. Select one source-clock hour below. Each region is drawn separately at the same hour and uses its full prepared extent. Road colours use seven log1p classes calculated across both regions and all hours. Grey links have missing flow. Diamonds mark CHP starts during the selected hour.

The 08:00 tables in the preparation section illustrate the conversion with a fixed worked example. The map and the highlighted points on the trend curves follow the time selected for this report.

4.1 Load the offline background

Load the two supplied OpenStreetMap backgrounds, one for Los Angeles and one for the Bay Area. The GeoJSON files were prepared from OpenFreeMap vector tiles. Their roads, water and place names provide context for the freeway measurements and CHP starts.

street_paths <- c("data/basemap-cache/los-angeles.geojson.gz", "data/basemap-cache/bay-area.geojson.gz")
basemap <- if (isTRUE(params$basemap)) read_case_streets(street_paths)

4.2 Los Angeles Area

plot_time <- params$plot_time
regions <- c("Los Angeles Area", "San Francisco Bay Area")
la_map <- traffic_flow_map(
  frames_path, time_label = plot_time, region = regions[1L], basemap = basemap,
  full_extent = TRUE, padding = 0.04
)

Los Angeles Area freeway flow and CHP starts in the selected hour.

4.3 San Francisco Bay Area

bay_map <- traffic_flow_map(
  frames_path, time_label = plot_time, region = regions[2L], basemap = basemap,
  full_extent = TRUE, padding = 0.04
)

San Francisco Bay Area freeway flow and CHP starts in the selected hour.

5 Results

The curves show mean freeway hourly flow for the two regions over the full day. Each hourly mean uses the available road values in that region. The dashed lines mark the hour shown on both maps.

5.1 Los Angeles Area

la_trend <- traffic_trend(frames, region = regions[1L])
plot(la_trend, metric = "mean", index = la_map$index,
     ylab = "Mean freeway flow (vehicles/hour)")

5.2 San Francisco Bay Area

bay_trend <- traffic_trend(frames, region = regions[2L])
plot(bay_trend, metric = "mean", index = bay_map$index,
     ylab = "Mean freeway flow (vehicles/hour)")

6 Export the results

Preparation saves its working files in a temporary directory. The draw calls use the current R graphics device. When running the blocks with Rscript and no device open, R can create Rplots.pdf in the working directory. To regenerate the report HTML and keep the selected maps and complete drawing data, run this command from the example directory:

Rscript run.R 08:00 --offline --export

Replace 08:00 with another prepared frame start to draw that frame. The default destination is a new output/ directory. To use a different new directory, add --output-dir NEW_DIRECTORY.

The command saves the selected maps at output/maps/pems-flow-los-angeles.png and output/maps/pems-flow-bay-area.png. output/prepared-data/flow-frames.rds contains all prepared frames and can be passed to the same plotting function to draw another frame. The directory also contains source.rds and input.rds, which record intermediate preparation steps.
